_what: Correction of the errors introduced by the DAC's mixed-domain conversion stage and by its analog stages - I/V, reconstruction filter, line driver. Not the digital stage.
_why_not_in_the_dac: Requires heavy DSP at the output rate, in the MHz range, and the DAC chip has no knowledge of the analog sections that follow it.
_preconditions: The device must be close to bit-perfect (direct DSD or NOS PCM).
A separate profile is needed per output rate, and per device setting that affects the output.
Built from a large number of analog-output measurements, iteratively. Time-consuming per DAC.
_who_benefits: "Better ones usually benefit more. So it is really more about improving DACs further, rather than fixing a bad one."
_cost: Author: "DAC correction can increase the load to 1.3x - 2x".
_for_us: We cannot build correction profiles - that needs lab measurement of each device. But the architecture should leave room for one, applied last, at the output rate. And the precondition is a field we already carry: a device that is not bit-exact cannot be corrected, which is one more reason to know that property.
_source: Interview with the author, Audiophile Style, 2026-11-11.
